subject: differential gene expresison - model predicts well, but with bad chain mixing/convergence

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: differential gene expresison - model predicts well, but with bad chain mixing/convergence
parts:
Hello Community,

I have a model of differential gene expression (e.g., clone of edgeR).

The model predicts well with good TP and FP rate similarly to the state of the art. The problem that the model have bad mix of the chains and does not converge nicely.

Could you community indicate some possible improvements?

P.S. sorry if the parameters are not in the Greek convention but I thought that the present way was better for understanding hyper-prior hierarchy





data {
    int<lower=1> G;                                       // number of genes
    int<lower=1> S;                                       // number of replicates
    vector[G] y[S];                                         // gene value
    int c[S];                                                  // map sample-treatment. There are just two treatments

}
parameters {
    vector<lower=0>[G] ex_mean[2];                // mean of a gene for all samples in a treatment
    vector<lower=0>[G] ex_sd[2];                    // standard deviation of a gene for all samples in a treatment

    //--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------//
    // ex_mean and ex_sd are correlated with an exp( linear function )
   //--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------//    

    vector<lower=0>[G] ex_mean_mean;          // for ex_mean of treatment 1 and 2. JUST TWO OBSERVATION FOR DEFINE THE MEAN
    vector<lower=0>[G] ex_mean_sd;              // for ex_mean of treatment 1 and 2. JUST TWO OBSERVATION FOR DEFINE THE SD

    //---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------//
    // ex_mean_mean and ex_mean_sd are correlated with an exp( linear function )
   //----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------//   

    real alpha;                                               //  parameter of the exp-linear function
    real<lower=0> beta;                                 //  parameter of the exp-linear function
    real<lower=0> shape;                              //  parameter of the exp-linear function
    real alpha2;                                             //  parameter of the exp-linear function
    real<lower=0> beta2;                               //  parameter of the exp-linear function
    real<lower=0> shape2;                            //  parameter of the exp-linear function
}
model {
    alpha ~ normal(0,0.1);                             //  must be close to 0
    beta ~ gamma(1.1, 10);                           // it's close to 0 but positive. if I use normal the sampler touches 0 and gives a warning
    shape ~ gamma(2,1);                              // it's close to 1 but positive. if I use normal the sampler touches 0 and gives a warning
                   
    alpha2 ~ normal(0,1);                              //  must be close to 0
    beta2 ~ gamma(1.1, 10);                         // it's close to 0 but positive. if I use normal the sampler touches 0 and gives a warning
    shape2 ~ gamma(2,1);                            // it's close to 1 but positive. if I use normal the sampler touches 0 and gives a warning

     for(s in 1:S) y[s] ~ normal(  ex_mean[c[s]], ex_sd[c[s]]  );
   
    //------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------//
    // every ex_mean_mean, ex_mean_sd is predicted just with
    // two values ex_mean treatment 1 gene 1, and treatment 2 gene 1
    //
    // Possible problem?
    //
    // the mean of gene 1 for two treatment is put under same prior because
    // the null hypothesis is that they are the same
    //-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------// 

     for(i in 1:2) ex_mean[i] ~ normal(ex_mean_mean, ex_mean_sd);              
     for(g in 1:G) for(i in 1:2) ex_sd[i, g] ~  gamma(shape, (shape / exp(alpha + (-beta * ex_mean[i, g]))));       

     ex_mean_mean ~ skew_normal(4.22, 2, 2.282);
     for(g in 1:G) ex_mean_sd[g] ~  gamma(shape2, (shape2 / exp(alpha2 + (-beta2 * ex_mean_mean[g]))));    
}

generated quantities {
    int<lower=0, upper=1> comparison [G,P];
    for (p in 1:P) for(g in 1:G) comparison[g,p] = ex_mean[1,p,g] > ex_mean[2,p,g];              // probability that each gene for treatment 1 is higher of tr.2
}



I also receive these warnings


The following numerical problems occured the indicated number of times after warmup on chain 2

Exception thrown at line 60: normal_log: Scale parameter[33] is 0, but must be > 0!             10

Exception thrown at line 57: normal_log: Scale parameter[59] is 0, but must be > 0!              2
Exception thrown at line 57: normal_log: Scale parameter[74] is 0, but must be > 0!              2
Exception thrown at line 66: gamma_log: Inverse scale parameter is 0, but must be > 0!           2
Exception thrown at line 66: gamma_log: Shape parameter is 0, but must be > 0!                   2

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] differential gene expresison - model predicts well, but with bad chain mixing/convergence
parts:
You probably want to try non-centered parameterizations
down at the lower level, such as here:

That's probably important for those gammas, too, but I don't know
how to do that off the top of my head (someone else probably does).

You can also try including some priors to keep those sd
parameters away from zero.

More generally, try turning adapt_delta up near 1 and see if
that helps with the numerical issues.

- Bob
